title: Particles of Chaos
subtitle: So let my dog explain it to you. After all, he isn't one to rely on intuition.

trails.title: The Actors Are in Place
trails.description: On this stage, there are no rewards ... only obligations.

Chapter Nine: Observer Instructions
P.S. If the observer cannot understand chapter one to eight, please read this chapter carefully.

1. All experiences generated by the device are limited to the mental or psychological realm. Do not confuse them with reality.
2. During the observation, please be mindful of your identity and act accordingly.
3. All pain experienced during the observation will be synchronized with your body. Please pay attention to your personal safety.
4. You will be disconnected from the device upon experiencing death. Please stay calm when returning to reality.

items.text: Laboratory environment initialized
Interferometer activated

Particle generation mode enabled 
Estimated particle consumption: 3.4 x 10^6
Temperature: 22°C, relative humidity: 65%

Observers in position
Loading vitals ...
Lorentz Lab

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's started to rain.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Oh my! We nearly walked into the rain without any protection! The Observer Instruction Book should've told us to bring our Equilibrium Umbrella.

items.speaker: X
items.text: No need for excess perspiration. The rain you're seeing is completely dissimilar to the "Storm."

items.speaker: X
items.text: Just a byproduct generated by this device, the Huygens-Fresnel Interferometer. It was built to observe the interaction between particular entities and chaotic systems.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: So this device about our heads ... is an interferometer?

items.speaker: X
items.text: That's right! We'll be utilizing it during our experiment, that to jog your memory—you volunteered for—Thanks for that, by the way.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Ms. Regulus and Ms. Sotheby already went in ahead of you. You'll probably find them in the world you're going to. Now, prepare for an enthralling adventure!
The two lab rats don't match the experimenter's enthusiasm.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The instruction book says this machine sends our minds to other worlds, and the destinations are particular to a time and place. Do I have that right?

items.speaker: X
items.text: Wow, you actually did your homework for once. Yep, it's true, these particular sorts of places have many names: quantum superpositions, simulated worlds, space-time bubbles ... Call it whatever you like.

items.speaker: X
items.text: I kind of like the name "Stage in the Rain."

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: "Stage in the Rain," sounds lovely! This APPLe can't wait to visit a new world.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Now, how do we begin? Are there any experimental procedures we must go through? Let me guess: "Close your eyes, take a deep breath, and walk clockwise in a circle three times" ...
X offers an amused laugh at APPLe's natural humor.

items.speaker: X
items.text: No need. Besides, how would I get you to "walk" in a circle?

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Well ... This APPLe doesn't see a problem.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: With that said, if you have no strict procedure, what exactly are you intending with this experiment? Is it a novel scientific experience, or just a jolly bit of fun?
X shrugs.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Oh. It's a serious experiment. One in which I propose to examine the very randomness that we usually attempt to avoid.

items.speaker: X
items.text: As you stand on the stage, breathing in and out ...

items.speaker: X
items.text: The raindrops' behavior should start to change.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Because I'm breathing on the stage?

items.speaker: X
items.text: More precisely, because you exist on the stage. Go ahead and touch the raindrops.
APPLe taps on one of the raindrops that hang in the air, as if it were a miniature heart.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: What ...?
The raindrops are chaotic at first but a pattern emerges as they bounce and spin before the red fruit, giving off a soft glow.
On the surface they could be mistaken for any other raindrop, yet ancient secrets hide within their apparent randomness.

items.speaker: X
items.text: See? You're so much more than an external spectator. You were able to affect the system.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Your actions, including your observations, no matter how inconsequential they may seem ...

items.speaker: X
items.text: ... can lead the system to produce unequivocally varied results. Alright, now ...
Numbers pop up on the screen at a blinding pace; X widens his eyes to keep track.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Loading complete, subjects in position ... Great.

items.speaker: X
items.text: See you later. Have fun.
Vitals loaded
Activating chaos particles:
Entering the Stage in the Rain
Nothing is true. Everything is permitted.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: *snore*
The snoring fruit's consciousness traveled through a dark, raining area to arrive where he is now. Just as the rain's patter disappears, he catches the sound of two distant voices.
And you're certain of this?
Unquestionably. Listen, what you hear now is the turbulence of air as it passes through its airway. As the soft tissues within vibrate they produce a familiar sound. It is "snoring."

This condition is commonly reckoned to be caused by a disorder of black bile in the body. Though, I would posit anatomically speaking, that it is nothing more than the relaxation of throat muscles during deep slumber.
We know what snoring is—what we want to know is how an apple can snore.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: *snore* Uh? Apple?
A strangely dressed man is standing by APPLe's side, surrounded by a group of soldiers. The wall they form has blocked all the exits.
With curiosity and caution in their eyes, the man and the soldiers stare at the helpless fruit, who has been pinned on the altar.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Erhm ... Good day, gentlemen. I believe I owe you thanks for this generous hospitality, unusual as it may be ...

items.speaker: Strange Man
items.text: Did you hear that? It appears to have spoken! If that's so, then no wonder it can snore.

items.speaker: Soldier
items.text: Enough. Speaking—snoring, it doesn't matter. We didn't hire you to lecture us on medicine.

items.speaker: Strange Man
items.text: "Hire," you say? That's odd way of putting it, after you cracked my ribs and hauled me here from Milan. I think some might instead call that "kidnapping."—I think I've caught a fever ...

items.speaker: Soldier
items.text: Stop whining: we barely bruised you! It was probably just the bumpy roads on the way to Firenze.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Firenze? Am I in Italy? Erhm, gentlemen, may I ask where I am and who you are?

items.speaker: Strange Man
items.text: You're the most curious apple I've ever known! Of course, we're in the great city of Firenze, Penisola Italiana.

items.speaker: Strange Man
items.text: These "gentlemen" you refer to here are known as the Templars. As for me ...

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: I am Leonardo of Vinci. Though, please call me Leonardo!

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Wait, Leonardo?
The sun shining in from the window illuminates the man's gentle smile.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: You're da Vinci?! Leonardo da Vinci, the great painter?

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: But please, as I said, I prefer just Leonardo.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: Leonardo the inventor, or Leonardo the engineer—perhaps even the anatomist? I should hope there is more to my reputation than just painting.
Leonardo's smile doesn't waver at all as the blade of his scalpel glints under the sunlight.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: Okay, it's safe to conclude you must be the mythical apple they've been looking for. I've never heard of any other talking apples.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: And I must conclude you are indeed THE Leonardo da Vinci.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Although ... If I might ask, Leonardo, what are you planning to do with that scalpel? And might this APPLe request you point it some other way?

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: You see, pointing a knife at someone is seen as somewhat unfriendly where I'm from.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: Please, do not worry, sir. This scalpel is a very delicate instrument, one of my favorites. Cold, sharp, and painless!

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: One swift cut, and it will find its way straight through the skin down to your core without spilling a drop of juice.
Leonardo leers closer to APPLe.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: Allow me to be honest with you and state things clearly: I have been asked to cut you into quarters so that I might record the make-up and consistency of your inner flesh—crisp, I'd wager.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: Next I'll soak you—I mean, your pieces—into a special solution so that I might ...

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: Oh, my apologies. I always get a bit excited whenever I start talking about my work. Now, hold still, Mr. Golden Apple ...
Leonardo reaches down toward the pinned APPLe, his smile increasingly less gentle and more wild.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: Just a little slice.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Stop this madness! I'll have you know what you're about to do is a severe violation of the Geneva Convention!

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: What the devil are you talking about? I'm growing more and more curious about you ...
The apple breaks free from his restraints and bounds around the room, but there is nowhere to hide, and the little fruit is eventually cornered.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Oh no ... Calm down! We can solve this in a civilized manner, can't we, like proper gentlemen?

items.speaker: Templar I
items.text: There is no need for propriety when dealing with witchcraft like whatever created you. Now, if you want to save yourself some pain, I suggest you stop.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: I feel like I'm in a nightmare! What in the world could you want with this APPLe for?

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: I can answer that. These "gentlemen" believe you to be the key to a rumored secret chamber.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: Of course, to prove their theory, they "hired" me to figure out just what it is that you are.
Leonardo bends down low; as if about to pick him up, but instead, he leans close and whispers.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: I don't intend to hurt you. Just cooperate for now. Help is on the way.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: ... Help?
Before APPLe can say more, Leonardo straightens up and shakes his head.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Oh. I do apologize, gentlemen. But I think there might have been a misunderstanding.

items.speaker: Templar Commander
items.text: You expect us to believe that?
An emotionless voice comes from the corner, followed by a towering man in armor.

items.speaker: Templar Commander
items.text: Perhaps you've forgotten.

items.speaker: Templar Commander
items.text: Months ago, a golden apple was found floating in the Arno by a fisherman.

items.speaker: Templar Commander
items.text: Being a faithful man, he brought it to the church. And there something strange happened.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Strange? What are you talking about? I'm only an apple.
The Templar commander raises his chin at Leonardo.

items.speaker: Templar Commander
items.text: You—Demonstrate for our guest.
Leonardo puts on a long face.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: I've already demonstrated it a dozen times ...
The towering man rests his hand on the sword at his waist, tilting it forward with intent.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: But of course, I would be glad to demonstrate once more, sir.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Whoa! Please be careful.
Leonardo picks up APPLe and paces the room, trying to find the right angle beneath the sunlight.
The soldiers are leaning against the wall, enjoying a reprieve from the heat outside.
As soon as Leonardo raises APPLe, however, they all stand straight and stare at him.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: Found it! The perfect angle!
Leonardo walks to the fresco, looking at the blurred faces of the figures on it.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Who are they?

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: Persons unknown.
Their identity is plainly a mystery to everyone in the room.
They do not appear to be the sort that would usually be recorded in the annals of history, and there is not even a subtle hint of their identity beyond their visage.
Nothing that might indicate the artist's intent in depicting them, nor in choosing to paint them in what can only be abject sorrow.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Is that all? According to this APPLe's experience, you should only need to cast an incantation to reveal the details.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: Call it magic, miracle, or trick as you like. All that I can see is a mystery that must be unraveled. Now wait ...

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: What for?

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: For the perfect ray of light.
When half the sun sinks below the horizon, a particular beam of light travels through the golden apple, turning into warm light spots.
As the light reaches the fresco, the blurred faces are suddenly illuminated.
And so the miracle is recreated—

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Blimey! What's going on?!

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: It's beyond me to explain what I am seeing here. I've examined both the wall and your skin for some time, but found nothing.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: This may truly be a miracle.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Gentlemen, there's a line of letters down there.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: Oh, it's nothing but a Caesar cipher. I can decode this in no time. Let me see ...

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: Sub cadente fulgore, cadentia sanctuaria coniunguntur.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: Under the waning glow, the waning sanctuaries unite.
